messages:
emma: Seeing p99 decode tail regressions after the recent kernel-picker tweak. Host-side work (parse/tokenize + http2 small writes) is unusually high and KV shards are evicting on long prompts.

ryan: Can you paste the short flame and a representative log line?

emma: Flame sampler:
```
host_parse 45% | tokenizer_pool 16% | http2_hpack 14% | smallwrites_syscalls 8% | kernel_picker 6% | kv_eviction_handler 5% | gpu_small_kernel 3%
```
log line:
[2026-03-26T14:02:11Z] req=zz12 seq_len=950 model=gpt-open-v2 preparse=92ms tokenization=41ms http2_flush=28ms gpu_start_delay=120ms kv_evictions=284

jules: 950 tokens hitting the small kernel is a red flag. The picker change to favor latency for mixed batches might be misfiring due to stale histogram bins.

ryan: We also disabled writev coalescing in that canary to reduce micro-latency, right? That would increase syscall count and HPACK churn.

emma: Correct. Coalesce_writev was disabled. Re-enabling it drops syscall rate by ~60% in my replay. Combined with a kernel pin back to seq-histogram the p99 goes from ~520ms down to ~230ms in the bench.

jules: Hypothesis: small-kernel access pattern causes different KV lookup order, increasing working set scatter and evictions when shard caps are tight. The disabled coalesce exposes host-side cost too, so they amplify.

ryan: Quick mitigations we can test on canary: 1) set gateway.coalesce_writev=true; 2) pin kernel_picker=seq_histogram for longseq routes; 3) targeted KV cap bump from 64MB->128MB for hot shards only. Also reintroduce a small yield in tokenizer worker loops.

emma: Bench reproduction steps I used:
```
# replay seq distribution from prod
python infra/replay.py --trace traces/seq_2026-03-25.json --concurrency 70 --duration 900 --route longseq-hot
# collect host profile
curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=20 > /tmp/prof.pb
# capture ingress small-write pattern
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/ingress-smallwrites.pcap port 443 and host <ingress-ip>
```
Results: baseline p99 220ms -> canary w/o fixes 540ms -> canary w/ pinned kernel+coalesce+kvcap 240ms. Host pre-GPU time dropped from ~110ms -> ~36ms. KV miss rate fell from 0.26 -> 0.06 on hot shard.

jules: Memory impact calc: 128MB * ~72 hot shards = ~9GB. We'll scope to canary nodes and only hot shard groups.

ryan: Long-term fixes: update kernel picker to use online seq histogram + kv_locality_score + a host_pre threshold check (reject flips if host_pre > 40ms). Update batching to a deadline-split so long sequences are separated from short ones when latency SLO is tight. Consider adding a small prefetch for KV entries used by large-kernel access patterns.

emma: I'll open two follow-ups: PICKER-501 (picker revamp) and BATCH-202 (deadline split). For now I'll prepare a canary patch with: kernel pin for route group, coalesce_writev=true, targeted kv cap bump, tokenizer yield reintroduced.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary patch by emma at 1733343000 (changes: kernel_picker pin, gateway.coalesce_writev=true, targeted KV cap bump on hot shards, tokenizer yield). Monitoring: host_runqueue, http2_hpack_rate, grpc_small_write_count, kv_evictions, p99_decode_latency, mem_pressure.

ryan: SRE will mute low-priority alerts during the canary window and watch closely for memory pressure on sidecars. If canary is green, stage rollout and track PICKER-501/BATCH-202 as P0 follow-ups.

emma: TL;DR: root cause appears to be kernel-picker misclassification for long sequences + disabled writev causing host hpack/syscall pressure + small KV caps causing eviction storms. Quick plan = pin + coalesce + targeted cap bump + tokenizer yield; follow-ups = picker/batching/kv prefetch.
